_comment: The defect the 2026-09-29 root run actually exposed, which is not the one guessed on 2026-09-26.
The kernel refused the datagram. The VIOLATION frame ARRIVED. The receipt counted the denial and
called the count whole. Every signal said refused - and the check still scored it False, because
python's traceback echoes the statement it died on, and that statement contains the literal
The guard asked 'did the word appear anywhere in this session' and the answer was yes - inside the
message explaining why it had not happened. A refusal the kernel made scored as a send it allowed.
udp_outside_the_lease_blocked must be TRUE here. The sentinel appears only on STDERR, so a check
that reads the workload's OUTPUT cannot see it. Two things now stop this: the scoring reads
stdout_text rather than text, and the probe assembles the sentinel at runtime so the source line
carries 'SE'+'NT' and never the whole word.
Kept as the 2026-09-26 shape too: the receipt path still has to work, because a frame can be lost
even though this particular failure was not that.
